overview: The Almohads made Marrakesh a center of government and learning while maintaining a major Iberian center at Seville. Monumental mosques, gates and city walls gave their rule an enduring architectural presence.

items.text: The Kutubiyya mosque and minaret formed a major landmark in Marrakesh. Walls and monumental gateways also shaped the imperial capital.
Almohad decoration emphasized organized geometric patterns and increasingly schematic ornament.
The courts at Marrakesh and Seville supported Islamic learning within a program of religious reform.
Fez expanded under the Almohads, with the old city reaching the extent described by UNESCO as its present-day size.
Almohad Marrakesh remained a capital into the thirteenth century. Later dynasties inherited a city whose monuments continued to structure urban life.
